overview: Health Preauthorisation Evidence Checklist addresses telemetry is noisy or missing, so operators spend time interpreting unrelated warnings in insurance operations. The first proof of value uses preauthorisation requests, benefit schedules and clinical documents. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is resubmission rate for missing evidence, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: preauthorisation requests, benefit schedules and clinical documents; define resubmission rate for missing evidence and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Chief Claims Officer / Chief Underwriter.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including inject sensor failures, stale data and dependency loss into the pilot.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
deliverables: Agreed test threshold for resubmission rate for missing evidence
